newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Novartis buys Merck unit.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Novartis buys Merck unit.

text.p: Novartis plans to acquire Merck's crop protection business for $910 million. The deal includes worldwide rights to the business, which had 1996 sales of $200 million. A full text of the companies' statement follows.
Novartis Acquires Merck's Crop Protection Business;

BASEL, Switzerland, May 13 /PRNewswire/ -- Novartis announced today the acquisition of Merck & Co., Inc.'s (NYSE: MRK) (located in Whitehouse Station, New Jersey) Crop Protection business for a price of USD 910 million. The deal includes the worldwide rights to Merck's business, which had 1996 sales of USD 200 million with a strong position in the high-value acaricide/insecticide and post-harvest fungicide markets. Also included are approximately USD 21 million in product inventories. Novartis has entered into a long-term supply agreement but will not be acquiring any of Merck's manufacturing plants.

According to Dr. Daniel Vasella, President of Novartis AG, "Novartis, with our strategic focus on life sciences and commitment to agribusiness, can achieve significant synergies and revenue enhancements in combining Merck's complementary product range with our ongoing crop protection business. We can look forward to dynamically growing this business through geographic expansion and new applications, capitalizing on opportunities for new formulations and combination products."

Merck is divesting the crop protection business as part of its decision to combine its Animal Health and Poultry Genetics business with Rhone Poulenc's Animal Health business to form a joint venture, Merial. The crop protection activities have been very consistently profitable. Sales have grown over the past four years at a compounded annual growth rate of 12 percent and gross profit and operating income have grown at a compounded annual growth rate of 12 and 13 percent respectively.

Novartis is a world leader in Life Sciences, with overall 1996 sales of CHF 27.6 billion (USD 19.0 billion) and ranked first in agribusiness with sales of CHF 7.6 billion (USD 5.2 billion, 73% in crop protection). The addition of Merck's crop protection activities will further strengthen Novartis' business, complementing the current, comprehensive activities in weed and disease control with a greatly enhanced presence in insecticides.

Merck's product line is primarily based on two active ingredients, abamectin and thiabendazole. Abamectin, which is sold primarily under the brand names AGRIMEK(R)/VERTIMEC(R), is an acaricide/insecticide with a unique mode of action. This characteristic enables it to control pest strains resistant to other active ingredients and to fit in well with resistance and integrated pest management programs. It is naturally derived, produced by fermentation, and used on high value crops (fruits and vegetables) as a high performance solution to intransigent pest problems. It provides superior knockdown and longer residual control than competitive products, yet is applied at low use rates. Thiabendazole, which is sold under the brand name MERTECT(R)/TECTO(R) is a premium post harvest fungicide.

Wolfgang Samo, head of Novartis' agribusiness activities stated, "Abamectin supplements our insecticide portfolio in an almost ideal way, adding an acaricide to our product line. This acquisition illustrates our commitment to sustainable agriculture, and will be an important element in our ongoing Integrated Pest Management programs and anti-resistance strategies."

The new products will be aggressively marketed as part of the worldwide Novartis crop protection portfolio. Sales will be supported by Novartis' well established sales network, marketing expertise and product development resources.

Novartis has the largest R&D budget in the life sciences industry, over CHF 3 billion (USD 2.1 billion) in 1996, and investing CHF 675 million in agribusiness R&D last year. There is a promising array of crop protection products in late stage development or the launch phase, most notably, Dual Magnum, Bicep Magnum, Action, and Expert. The company has an active research program in biotechnology and chemistry. Using these technologies together provides growers with more options for developing IPM strategies and dealing with potential resistance challenges. With the acquisition, Novartis will gain several development compounds, including a high potential insecticide quite close to market introduction.
The closing of the deal is subject to government approvals and other customary closing conditions.

Novartis is a world leader in Life Sciences with its core businesses in Healthcare, Agribusiness and Nutrition. In 1996, Novartis achieved Group sales in Life Sciences of 27.6 billion Swiss Francs and invested more than 3 billion Swiss Francs in research and development. Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, Novartis employs a workforce of about 90,000 in more than 100 countries around the world. SOURCE Novartis AG
